# Horror audio

- Ambient horror — techiew, CC0. https://opengameart.org/content/ambient-horror
  Download: https://opengameart.org/sites/default/files/ambient_horror_0.ogg
- Long Sci-fi Sting — Fupi, CC0. https://opengameart.org/content/long-sci-fi-sting
  Download: https://opengameart.org/sites/default/files/longscifisting_2.ogg

- Evil creature — A New Room, submitted by qubodup, CC0. https://opengameart.org/content/evil-creature
  Download: https://opengameart.org/sites/default/files/ambient%20sound%20fx.zip
  The five tracks were losslessly extracted from the original Audacity project's 16-bit PCM blocks to creature_01.wav through creature_05.wav using tools/extract_creature_audio.ps1.

Existing undead and door sounds are also played spatially with varying pitch.

- Heartbeat sounds — bart, CC0. https://opengameart.org/content/heartbeat-sounds
  heartbeat_slow_0.wav is looped with fear-dependent pitch and volume.
- Horror breathing — primbal, CC0. https://opengameart.org/content/horror-breathing
  Original OGG recording played sparingly near the listener at elevated fear.

Design references (not a claim to measure hormones):
- Arnal et al., Human Screams Occupy a Privileged Niche in the Communication Soundscape (2015): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4562283/
- Auditory roughness elicits defense reactions: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7806762/

Implementation uses approaching spatial cues, contrasting quiet periods, irregular event spacing, rough creature vocalizations, and an accelerating recorded heartbeat. Fear is a gameplay meter, not a biological measurement. No inaudible frequency or guaranteed physiological effect is claimed.
